sources.entry: zvec - A lightweight, in-process vector database that embeds directly into applications.

summary.one_liner: Zvec is an open-source, in-process vector database that embeds directly into applications, with low-latency similarity search and minimal setup.
summary.what_it_does: Zvec runs as a library inside your application process rather than as a separate server. You define a collection schema with vector fields, insert documents with vector values, and run similarity queries through the Python API shown in the README. The README describes support for dense and sparse vectors, multi-vector queries, several vector index types spanning memory and disk, full-text search over string fields, and hybrid queries that combine vector similarity, full-text search, and structured filters. Storage uses write-ahead logging for persistence. Multiple processes can read the same collection at once, but writes are single-process exclusive. Official SDKs are listed for Python, Node.js, Go, Rust, Java, and Dart/Flutter.
use_cases: local vector search in notebooks or CLI tools
hybrid search combining vectors, keywords and filters
on-device vector search on mobile or edge
Chinese full-text search over string fields
notable: Runs in-process with no server or configuration, per the README
Write-ahead logging for durable storage across crashes and power loss
Multiple concurrent readers on one collection, with single-process writes
Built-in full-text search and hybrid queries that fuse vector, keyword and filter conditions
Embedded Jieba dictionary and HMM model for Chinese tokenization in v0.8.0
caveats: Writes are single-process exclusive, so concurrent writers are not supported
Python requires 64-bit Python 3.10-3.14; Java requires Java 8+
The README notes that uniform quantization can increase error and reduce recall
Stack is not fully specified in the README; the C++ core is inferred from the build-from-source reference and is not stated explicitly
